title: Scalar transport and refinement descent of normalized semilinear exchange
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, with Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; $g,g'$ need not be $k$-linear. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with induced isomorphism $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the chosen-compactification finite and integral exchange transformations $e_\Lambda^c$ and coefficient comparisons of [def-exchange-projection], the actual strict integral lift of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], and the raw rational and common-stage categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Suppose the finite and integral transformations have been identified with the ordered proper/open reindexing maps, with their identity, successive-isomorphism, vertical-composition and coefficient-reduction equations; at the integral stage assume these identifications and equations hold on the actual strict reduction diagrams before $R\lim$. All hypotheses here concern these specified maps, not independently chosen exchange isomorphisms.

Then scalar localization carries the integral two-factor identity and its pasting equations to the identical ordered reindexing identities and equations for $e_E^c$. The supplied scalar-extension comparisons carry this map to $e_L^c$ for every further finite coefficient field $L/E$ on their stated coefficient domains. These identifications satisfy the identity and finite-field-tower cocycles, hence give the same ordered identity and pasting equations for $e_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}^c$ in the common-stage category. This uses only integral reduction before localization, and asserts no reduction operation on rational coefficients.

At every stage $\Lambda\in\{A_n,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ restrict to the compactification-independent field-base domains, including the witness, lattice, constructibility and amplitude requirements, of [fix-lem-exchanges](4). For a refinement $a:c_1\to c_2$ and its isomorphism base change $a':c_1'\to c_2'$, let $C_a:F_{c_2}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_1}$ and $C_{a'}:F_{c_2'}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_1'}$ be the canonical refinement comparisons, where $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ at finite coefficients and its specified completed/localized/common-stage form at higher stages. Then
$$e^{c_1}(G_gC_a)=(C_{a'}G_{g'})e^{c_2}.$$
The same equation holds for canonical changes of compactification through a common refinement. For a compatible composition tower these identifications intertwine its canonical compact-support compositor and are unchanged under refinement of that tower, with the normalized proper/open maps of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] and [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-composition-pasting-coherence]. Thus the reindexing identity and pasting equations descend through exactly the compactification comparisons supplied by [fix-lem-exchanges](4), even when the base-change isomorphisms are not $k$-linear.

proof.text:
Write the assumed integral identity as $e_R^c=R p'_*(\beta_R)r_R$, where $R=\mathcal O_E$, and let $Q_T$ denote scalar localization. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] with identical coefficient rings to the operation functors, $r_R,\beta_R$ and their whiskerings. The specified rational map is the localized integral map by [def-exchange-projection], so
$$e_E^c=Q(e_R^c)=R p'_{*,E}(Q\beta_R)Q(r_R).$$
This is the ordered rational reindexing identity. For a localized arrow $v/\varpi_E^m$, naturality is the integral naturality equation multiplied by $\varpi_E^{-m}$; hence it holds on every localized arrow. The lemma preserves identities, composition and both whiskerings, so applying it to each assumed identity, successive-base-change and vertical-pasting equation gives that same equation at $E$. Its inverse-map clause preserves all comparison isomorphisms. No finite reduction is performed after localization.

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$ let $T_T=-\otimes_E L$ and write $J_F:T_{Y'}F_E\cong F_LT_X$ and $J_H:T_{Y'}H_E\cong H_LT_X$, where $F_E=G_gF_{c,E}$ and $H_E=F_{c',E}G_{g'}$. The supplied comparisons of [def-exchange-projection] intertwine pullback composition, proper units and counits, and the canonical open comparison. Expand the proper mate into unit, square identification, counit. Move $T$ across these three arrows in that order using the supplied three commutative squares, then across the open arrow. The target comparison of each arrow cancels the inverse source comparison of the next. The resulting outer square is
$$J_H\,T_{Y'}(e_E^c)=e_L^c\,J_F.$$
The same cancellation with $r_E,\beta_E$ in place of the mate gives their corresponding ordered comparisons. Thus the two-factor formula at $E$ becomes precisely the one at $L$. This uses supplied comparison equations, not mere existence of isomorphic functors. Their identity and field-tower cocycles imply the same cocycle for these four-arrow composites: for $E\subset L\subset M$, the intermediate $J$ and $J^{-1}$ cancel, leaving the direct $E\subset M$ comparison.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. At an object $(E,K)$ represent the exchange by $e_{E,K}^c$. For an arrow represented by $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}N$, enlarge all data to $M$. Step 2 identifies the source and target scalar comparisons with those for $e_M^c$, so naturality is exactly $H_M(u)e_{M,TK}^c=e_{M,TN}^cF_M(u)$. After any further field extension both sides give the same representatives by the tower equation of Step 2. Hence the class is independent of stage and defines the common-stage exchange. Every required equation involves only finitely many arrows, so choose one field containing their stages and apply the equation there, already established in Steps 1--2. Equality at that field implies equality of classes. This gives the same ordered formula, identity and pasting equations in the actual common-stage category, without adjoining retracts.

Invertibility of the coefficient prime is coefficientPrime_isUnit_stalk. Pull these field-base structures across the isomorphism g prime. The finite-extension base-change theorem then gives the constructible source witness for c2 and target witness for c1. Apply completeCompactSupportProetale_refinement to the given lattice and compatible origins, then apply congrArg for finiteExtensionRationalArrow. Its two further functor images are obtained by congrArg for the specified inverse coefficient equivalences and common-stage inclusion.
